name: Create blog post
description: Create blog post Creates a new blog post in the space specified by the spaceId. POST /wiki/api/v2/blogposts
context:
POST /wiki/api/v2/blogposts
Creates a new blog post in the space specified by the spaceId. By default this will create the blog post as a non-draft, unless the status is specified as draft. If creating a non-draft, the title must not be empty. Currently only supports the storage representation specified in the body.representation enums below
Required: body (body)
Optional: private (query) — The blog post will be private. Only the user who creates this blog post will have permission to view and edit one.

name: Delete blog post
description: Delete blog post Delete a blog post by id. DELETE /wiki/api/v2/blogposts/{id}
context:
DELETE /wiki/api/v2/blogposts/{id}
Delete a blog post by id. By default this will delete blog posts that are non-drafts. To delete a blog post that is a draft, the endpoint must be called on a draft with the following param `draft=true`. Discarded drafts are not sent to the trash and are permanently deleted. Deleting a blog post that is not a draft moves the blog post to the trash, where it can be restored later. To permanently delete a blog post (or "purge" it), the endpoint must be called on a **trashed** blog post with the following param `purge=true`. **[Permissions](https://support.atlassian.com/confluence-cloud/docs/what-are-confluences-roles/) required**: Permission to view the blog post and its corresponding space. Permission to delete blog posts in the space. [`manage/content`](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/confluence/rest/v2/api-group-space-permissions/#api-space-permissions-get) permission for the space (if attempting to purge). **Note:** To find the display name for each permission ID, call the [Get available space permissions](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/confluence/rest/v2/api-group-space-permissions/#api-space-permissions-get) API.
Required: id (path) — The ID of the blog post to be deleted.
Optional: purge (query) — If attempting to purge the blog post.; draft (query) — If attempting to delete a blog post that is a draft.

name: Get attachments for blog post
description: Get attachments for blog post Returns the attachments of specific blog post. GET /wiki/api/v2/blogposts/{id}/attachments
context:
GET /wiki/api/v2/blogposts/{id}/attachments
Returns the attachments of specific blog post. The number of results is limited by the `limit` parameter and additional results (if available) will be available through the `next` URL present in the `Link` response header. **[Permissions](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/_AozKw) required**: Permission to view the content of the blog post and its corresponding space.
Required: id (path) — The ID of the blog post for which attachments should be returned.
Optional: sort (query) — Used to sort the result by a particular field.; cursor (query) — Used for pagination, this opaque cursor will be returned in the `next` URL in the `Link` response header. Use the relative URL in the `Link` header to retrieve the `next` set of results.; status (query) — Filter the results to attachments based on their status. By default, `current` and `archived` are used.; mediaType (query) — Filters on the mediaType of attachments. Only one may be specified.; filename (query) — Filters on the file-name of attachments. Only one may be specified.; limit (query) — Maximum number of attachments per result to return. If more results exist, use the `Link` header to retrieve a relative URL that will return the next set of results.

name: Get blog post by id
description: Get blog post by id Returns a specific blog post. GET /wiki/api/v2/blogposts/{id}
context:
GET /wiki/api/v2/blogposts/{id}
Returns a specific blog post. **[Permissions](https://confluence.atlassian.com/x/_AozKw) required**: Permission to view the blog post and its corresponding space.
Required: id (path) — The ID of the blog post to be returned. If you don't know the blog post ID, use Get blog posts and filter the results.
Optional: body-format (query) — The content format types to be returned in the `body` field of the response. If available, the representation will be available under a response field of the same name under the `body` field.; get-draft (query) — Retrieve the draft version of this blog post.; status (query) — Filter the blog post being retrieved by its status.; version (query) — Allows you to retrieve a previously published version. Specify the previous version's number to retrieve its details.; include-labels (query) — Includes labels associated with this blog post in the response. The number of results will be limited to 50 and sorted in the default sort order. A `meta` and `_links` property will be present to indicate if more results are available and a link to retrieve the rest of the results.; include-properties (query) — Includes content properties associated with this blog post in the response. The number of results will be limited to 50 and sorted in the default sort order. A `meta` and `_links` property will be present to indicate if more results are available and a link to retrieve the rest of the results.; include-operations (query) — Includes operations associated with this blog post in the response, as defined in the `Operation` object. The number of results will be limited to 50 and sorted in the default sort order. A `meta` and `_links` property will be present to indicate if more results are available and a link to retrieve the rest of the results.; include-likes (query) — Includes likes associated with this blog post in the response. The number of results will be limited to 50 and sorted in the default sort order. A `meta` and `_links` property will be present to indicate if more results are available and a link to retrieve the rest of the results.; include-versions (query) — Includes versions associated with this blog post in the response. The number of results will be limited to 50 and sorted in the default sort order. A `meta` and `_links` property will be present to indicate if more results are available and a link to retrieve the rest of the results.; include-version (query) — Includes the current version associated with this blog post in the response. By default this is included and can be omitted by setting the value to `false`.; include-favorited-by-current-user-status (query) — Includes whether this blog post has been favorited by the current user.; include-webresources (query) — Includes web resources that can be used to render blog post content on a client.; include-collaborators (query) — Includes collaborators on the blog post.

name: Redact Content in a Confluence Blog Post
description: Redact Content in a Confluence Blog Post Redacts sensitive content in a Confluence blog post by replacing specified text ranges with redaction markers. POST /wiki/api/v2/blogposts/{id}/redact
context:
POST /wiki/api/v2/blogposts/{id}/redact
Redacts sensitive content in a Confluence blog post by replacing specified text ranges with redaction markers. Each redaction in the response includes a unique UUID for restoration (except code block redactions). The response metadata items maintain the same order as the input redaction pointers, and completely overlapping redactions are merged into a single redaction with one UUID. **Note**: This endpoint requires **Atlassian Guard Premium**.
Required: id (path) — The ID of the blog post to redact content from.
Optional: body (body)
